international.headline: SCO leaders adopt the Bishkek Declaration at the 26th summit
facts: The 26th Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Summit took place in Bishkek, Kyrgyzstan, from August 31 to September 1, 2026; its theme was “25 Years of the SCO: Together Towards Sustainable Peace, Development and Prosperity.”
The summit adopted the Bishkek Declaration, four memoranda of understanding covering climate, nuclear safety, energy security and drug control, and more than 20 other decisions and declarations.
Members agreed on joint measures to counter drug threats and prevent the spread of synthetic drugs until 2030.
The summit called for cooperation on biodiversity, an SCO Green Technology Corridor and emerging technologies including regional data centres and artificial intelligence.
The SCO was established on June 15, 2001, in Shanghai; its headquarters are in Beijing, China, and its official languages are Chinese and Russian.
As stated in the notes, the SCO had 10 members in 2026; India and Pakistan joined in 2017, Iran in 2023 and Belarus in July 2024.
international.summary: The summit adopted the Bishkek Declaration and agreements spanning regional security, sustainability and technology cooperation.
international.staticLink: The SCO originated from the Shanghai Five, formed in 1996; its founding members in 2001 were China, Russia, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan.
international.prelimsTakeaway: The 26th SCO Summit was hosted in Bishkek and concluded with the Bishkek Declaration.
international.mainsAngle: Examine the SCO’s role in combining regional security cooperation with climate, biodiversity and technology agendas.

international.canonicalTopic: Lionel Messi retires from international football
international.headline: Lionel Messi announces retirement from international football
facts: Lionel Messi announced his retirement from international football on August 31, 2026, after a 21-year international career; he will continue playing for Inter Miami.
The notes give his Argentina record as 207 appearances and 125 goals.
Argentina’s honours under Messi’s leadership include the 2022 FIFA World Cup and the 2021 and 2024 Copa América titles; the notes say Argentina finished runner-up at the 2026 FIFA World Cup.

national.headline: Government notifies ₹1,27,500 crore Semicon 2.0 scheme
facts: The Union Government notified Semicon 2.0, the second phase of the Semicon India Programme, on 2026-08-31 with an allocation of ₹1,27,500 crore.

The scheme seeks to build a domestic semiconductor ecosystem spanning chip design, manufacturing, packaging, research and skills, through six pillars: Design; Machines and Materials; Fabrication Units; ATMP and OSAT; Research and Development; Talent Development.

Silicon wafer fabrication units with a minimum investment of ₹20,000 crore are eligible for 40% financial assistance; compound semiconductor, display and other specialised fabrication units are eligible for 35%.
The Deployment-Linked Incentive provides 9% of net sales for up to five years, capped at ₹30 crore per application.
The notes report around 85,000 semiconductor engineers already trained and a target of training an additional one lakh people.
The nodal ministry is MeitY and the implementing agency is the India Semiconductor Mission; the Semicon India Programme was approved in 2021.
national.summary: Semicon 2.0 was notified with an allocation of ₹1,27,500 crore to expand domestic semiconductor design, manufacturing, packaging, research and talent development.
national.staticLink: Semiconductor manufacturing ecosystem: fabrication, ATMP and OSAT.
national.prelimsTakeaway: Silicon wafer fabrication units meeting the stated minimum investment threshold may receive 40% assistance; specialised fabrication units may receive 35%.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss the strategic and economic case for building domestic semiconductor capabilities, including supply-chain resilience, skills and implementation risks.

national.canonicalTopic: Memorable Trials Unforgettable Cases book release
national.headline: ‘Memorable Trials, Unforgettable Cases’ released in Kannada and English
facts: Karnataka Minister for School Education and Literacy Madhu Bangarappa released the Kannada and English editions in Shivamogga on August 31, 2026.
The book was written by former Karnataka High Court Judge Justice H.N. Nagamohan Das and published by Jana Prakashana.
Its subjects include constitutional awareness, judicial experience and significant cases and trials from the author’s career.

national.headline: MoSPI releases National Accounts Statistics–2026
facts: The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation released National Accounts Statistics–2026 on August 31, 2026; it contains 60 statistical statements on national income and macroeconomic indicators.
The publication includes final estimates for 2022–23 and 2023–24, first revised estimates for 2024–25 and revised macroeconomic indicators for 2025–26.
The revised real GDP growth figures listed are 7.3% for 2023–24, 7.2% for 2024–25 and 7.8% for 2025–26.
The corresponding nominal GDP growth figures are 11.1%, 9.4% and 8.6%.
national.summary: MoSPI’s 2026 national-accounts publication provided revised GDP estimates and other macroeconomic series.
national.staticLink: National accounts compile measures of national income and related economic indicators.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The notes list revised real GDP growth of 7.8% for 2025–26 and nominal GDP growth of 8.6% for that year.
national.mainsAngle: Revised national-accounts data informs assessment of economic growth and the evidence base for policy planning.

national.headline: Bihar and Jharkhand plan an agreement on Son River water allocation
facts: Bihar and Jharkhand were set to sign a Son River water-sharing agreement on August 31, 2026; the notes describe the dispute as continuing for nearly 25 years after Jharkhand’s creation in November 2000.
The stated allocation is 5.75 million acre-feet for Bihar and 2.0 million acre-feet for Jharkhand, totalling 7.75 million acre-feet.
The total corresponds to undivided Bihar’s allocation under the 1973 Bansagar Agreement, concluded among Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and undivided Bihar.
The Son originates in the Amarkantak Plateau, flows through Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Jharkhand and Bihar, and joins the Ganga west of Patna.
national.summary: The proposed agreement would formally divide the Son water share previously allocated to undivided Bihar between its successor states.
national.prelimsTakeaway: The stated allocation is 5.75 million acre-feet to Bihar and 2.0 million acre-feet to Jharkhand; the 1973 Bansagar Agreement involved Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and undivided Bihar.
national.mainsAngle: Discuss inter-state river-water allocation, successor-state arrangements and the role of agreements in irrigation and water security.
